title: What Does 'Accessible Information' Actually Mean?
assessmentMethod: Private reflective journal entry, not scored

body.en: A climate warning printed only in small English text on a notice board is information — but it isn't accessible information. Accessible means it reaches people through more than one channel and format: plain language alongside technical terms, audio alongside text, high-contrast visuals, sign language alongside spoken announcements. It's the difference between information existing and information actually reaching everyone it's meant for. Think about how you've received climate or weather information recently — a radio announcement, a poster, a phone alert. If you couldn't see, hear, or read that format, would the information have reached you at all?
